column1: # Setting patches (dm/games/README.md, Setting patches): words of the game's code the host writes at launch when a setting has a value, each after checking the original word on the build it was found in.
# MetalFX as the only anti-aliasing (DM_UPSCALER=metalfx-temporal, no row of its own; README.md, Anti-aliasing). NDSR's SMAA is three compute dispatches ahead of the network, all in
# main+0x14e3720: edge detection, blend weights (indirect, over the edge list), and a compose that writes the network's input. main+0x14e3660 clears the weights each frame, so with the
# first two left out the compose copies the scene: MetalFX takes it with its sub-pixel detail, and only spatial and Game keep SMAA. These rows stay ahead of DM_UPSCALE_RATIO's, whose
# native-mfx rows test this variable (a term on a variable with rows of its own tests what it wrote)

column1: # Render resolution (README.md, Upscaler and resolution). The scene is the output (2560x1440 docked, 1920x1080 handheld) times a scale the dynamic-resolution controller picks each
# frame from its level palette (RomFS ModelSceneExtensionParam: 0.75 down to 0.333 docked, to 0.4445 handheld; never 1.0), built at stage start from the palette's level entries
# (main+0x31c3b30: {scale, priority} nodes in a list at ctrl+0x190). The controller's update (main+0x805aa0) returns the scale in the low word of x0 with a level-changed flag above
# it, which its caller (main+0x31d3ee0) turns into the scene's scale (ctrl+0xe5c) whenever the level changes or the stage starts. Both of its paths return through main+0x805ff0
# (fmov w9,s8: the chosen level's scale, aligned to the controller's width step). A fixed render resolution writes the scale there (movz w9,#hi,lsl #16: the float's upper half,
# so 1.5 is 0.66797 and 1.6875 0.59375): every level then has that scale. At rate 1.0 the game's network still runs, 1:1, so with MetalFX's temporal scaler that dispatch is drawn at the
# output's size: Native (MetalFX AA), native-mfx, is the same word
# Dynamic (DM_UPSCALE_DYNAMIC=1): the controller keeps stepping through its levels, and a map s' = a s + b takes its palette's 0.75 .. 0.33334 onto the sharpest's scale .. the softest's (handheld's

# last level, 0.4445, stops short of the softest). The map is applied to each level as the list is built, so the sizes the controller predicts a level's load from are the sizes drawn: mapped after the
# update it took Native for its 1080-line level 0 and stayed there at any load. The map runs in the padding after the update (main+0x8065c4-0x8065dc, seven zero words: no branch enters them), reached

# from the builder's load of a level's scale, main+0x31c3cb0 (ldr w26,[x0]): ldr d1,<the last two words>; ldr s2,[x0]; fmla s1,s2,v1.s[1]; fmov w26,s1; b main+0x31c3cb4; b; a. The sharpest's rows write

# the five instructions, the softest's the two constants and the branch in, so the branch is written only with the constants; a softest at or sharper than the sharpest is a = 0, the padding's own word.

# With MetalFX's temporal scaler the softest's rows also set what the controller works to (README.md, Render resolution): its load threshold (main+0x31c3bdc, 0x31c3be4, in place of the stage parameter's
# 95), since the time it reads leaves out the scaler, and how long a sharper level must have room before it is taken (main+0x31c3bfc, in place of 30 frames), since its load is noisy at low sizes
